open_points.subject: M26 AllocationInstruction amount validation
open_points.text: M26 says “an individual amount is not otherwise constrained (zero and negative amounts are accepted and stored)”, while the modeling convention requires money to have “2 fraction digits”, A9 says “stored amounts are already 2-digit exact”, and R0-05 says money is “rounded half up to two places”.
open_points.question: When an allocation amount has more than two fraction digits, must it be rejected, rounded before sum validation and storage, or accepted and stored exactly?
options: Reject allocation amounts that do not already have exactly two fraction digits.
Round each allocation amount ROUND_HALF_UP to two digits before validating the sum and storing it.
Accept and store the supplied arbitrary-precision Decimal because individual allocation amounts are otherwise unconstrained.
open_points.default_guess: Reject amounts that are not already exact two-fraction-digit EUR values.

witness.initial: An active project has an included expense with total_amount 100.00.
events: An authorized operator replaces its allocations with explicit amounts 100.005 and -0.005, whose supplied exact sum is 100.000.
outcomes: The operation is refused because neither amount is already a two-fraction-digit stored money value.
The operation succeeds after rounding and stores 100.01 and -0.01; alternatively, a literal reading of M26 stores 100.005 and -0.005 unchanged.
witness.observer: The operator sees either a refusal or a successful allocation view containing values different from—or more precise than—the submitted two-decimal money policy.
